Assignment of samples to units of a self-organising map

Source: R/som_functions.R
eemsom_samples.Rd

Assignment of samples to units of a self-organising map

Usage

eemsom_samples(som)

Arguments

som

object of class eemsom, see eemsom

Value

data frame with columns sample, unit (number of the best matching unit), x and y (position of the unit on the map), distance (Euclidean distance between sample and prototype), hits (number of samples mapped to the unit), umatrix (mean distance between the prototype of the unit and the prototypes of its neighbours, see eemsom_plot_map) and cluster (NA if no clustering was done)

Details

With missing values (na = "keep"), the distances are calculated from the available wavelength pairs of a sample and scaled up to the number of all wavelength pairs, as in kohonen.

The columns hits and umatrix help to find unusual samples (outliers): such samples often occupy a unit alone (hits = 1) that is separated from its neighbours by a high U-matrix value. Their distance to the prototype can be small though, because the prototype adapts to them. The leave-one-out distance calculated by eemsom_stability with type = "loo" is a more reliable indicator.

See also

Other map results: eemsom_codes(), eemsom_predict(), eemsom_quality(), eemsom_split()

Examples

data(eem_list)

som <- eemsom(eem_list, rlen = 100, seed = 42)
eemsom_samples(som)
